about: datum's shell-style tokenizer, as one list of cases read by both sides.
`web/src/lib/shellSplit.ts::shellSplit` have to tokenize a REPL line
identically, or a command means one thing in the terminal and another in
the browser. They used to diverge at exactly two codepoints, because each
borrowed its host language's idea of whitespace instead of stating datum's:
U+0085 NEL is whitespace to Rust and not to JavaScript, U+FEFF is
whitespace to JavaScript and not to Rust (da-rx63).
Two hand-written test files drift the same way two implementations do, so
the cases live here and both suites read this file:
`web/tests/shellsplit.test.mjs`. Add a case here, not there.
Every non-ASCII character is written as a \uXXXX escape on purpose: a
literal invisible character in a fixture is one the next reader cannot see.

cases.name: a run of ASCII whitespace is one separator
a backslash inside double quotes lets the next character through
a bare backslash escapes the next character
an unterminated quote closes at end of line
an empty quoted token is a token
U+0085 NEL separates - Rust said yes, JavaScript said no
U+FEFF leading BOM separates - JavaScript said yes, Rust said no
the narrow, medium, ogham and line/paragraph separators separate
cases.line: occur a b c d e

cases.name: en quad through hair space separate
U+200B zero-width space is not whitespace and stays in its token
whitespace inside quotes is kept, NEL and BOM included
a line of nothing but whitespace is no tokens
